666	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

668	    JacobianWitness C :=
669	  haveI : GeometricallyIntegral C.hom := geometricallyIntegral_of_curve C
670	  haveI := Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint C
671	  { J := Scheme.Pic0Scheme C
672	    grpObj := (Scheme.Pic0.grpObj C).some
673	    proper := Scheme.Pic0.proper C
674	    smooth := Scheme.Pic0.smooth C
675	    geomIrred := Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible C
676	    smoothGenus := smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0 C
677	    isAlbaneseFor := fun P => isAlbanese_pic0 C _ _ _ _ P }
678	
679	/-- The Albanese witness for a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve `C`,
680	constructed **uniformly in the genus** as the identity component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` of the
681	Picard scheme of `C`.
682	
683	By the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*`), `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is representable
684	(`Scheme.PicScheme.representable`) and is an abelian variety of dimension `genus C`:
685	its tangent space at the identity is `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` (`Scheme.Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`),
686	giving smoothness of relative dimension `genus C` (`Scheme.Pic0.smooth`), properness
687	(`Scheme.Pic0.proper`), and geometric irreducibility
688	(`Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible`); the Albanese universal property is the
689	Abel–Jacobi factorisation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.AlbaneseUP`.
690	
691	The genus-`0` case is **not** special and needs no separate construction: when
692	`genus C = 0` the tangent space is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
693	automatically, and the universal property degenerates to the (then trivial) statement
694	that every pointed morphism `C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety is constant. The former
695	`genusZeroWitness` / `positiveGenusWitness` genus split — together with its bespoke
696	rigidity / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery — has been
697	removed in favour of this single uniform witness.
698	
699	**No hypothesis on `C(k)`.** The binders are exactly the three challenge hypotheses, which
700	is the owner decision of 2026-07-28 (protection I-0491) and the full strength the challenge
701	asks for. This is *not* a specialisation of
702	`picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`: it is wired to the **étale** Picard development,
703	with underlying scheme `Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C` — the identity component of the scheme
704	representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor (`Picard/Pic0Et.lean`,
705	`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`). Sheafifying is what removes the rational point:
706	the unsheafified functor is not a sheaf, so representability of it over an arbitrary field
707	would be a *false* statement rather than an unproved one.
708	
709	Four of the six witness fields come from theorems that are proved **unconditionally** and
710	measure axiom-clean (`Pic0Et.grpObj`, `Pic0Et.geometricallyIrreducible`, and through them
711	`Pic0Et.locallyOfFiniteType` / `Pic0Et.isSeparated`). This definition carries no `sorry` of
712	its own, but that is a statement about this file, not a completeness claim: it depends on
713	the five obligations enumerated in the file header —
714	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`, `Scheme.Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced`,
715	`Scheme.Pic0Et.universallyClosed`, `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et` and
716	`isAlbanese_pic0Et` — every one of which is a **true statement awaiting a proof**. The
717	`GeometricallyIntegral` hypothesis of the Picard development is *not* among them: it is
718	synthesised from the challenge hypotheses through `Smooth.geometricallyIntegral` (see
719	`geometricallyIntegral_of_curve`). -/
720	noncomputable def picardJacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
721	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
722	    JacobianWitness C where
723	  J := Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C
724	  grpObj := (Scheme.Pic0Et.grpObj C).some
725	  proper := Scheme.Pic0Et.proper C
726	  smooth := Scheme.Pic0Et.smooth C
727	  geomIrred := Scheme.Pic0Et.geometricallyIrreducible C
728	  smoothGenus := smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et C
729	  isAlbaneseFor := fun P => isAlbanese_pic0Et C _ _ _ _ P
730	
731	/-- **The witness over an algebraically closed field: a genuine `k̄` theorem.**
732	
733	The same assembly as `picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`, with the rational point
734	supplied by the theorem `hasRationalPoint_of_curve_of_isAlgClosed` rather than assumed. Over
735	`k̄` a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve really does have a rational point — the
736	curve is a nonempty Jacobson space and its closed points are rational — so this definition
737	records what the `picSharp` route actually reaches, with nothing false anywhere in it.
738	
739	**It is not the headline** (owner decision of 2026-07-28, protection I-0491 clause 4). It is
740	a theorem about algebraically closed base fields, and the challenge asks for an arbitrary
741	one; that statement is `picardJacobianWitness`, which is built on the étale-sheafified
742	functor and does not pass through this definition or through
743	`picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`.
744	
745	Its obligations are those of the `picSharp` route with the rational point discharged:
746	`Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`'s content (i.e. `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`),
747	`Pic0.smooth`, `Pic0.proper`, and the two `picSharp`-shaped leaves
748	`smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0` / `isAlbanese_pic0`. Discharging the rational point
749	does not remove the representability gate — it makes it *fire* instead of being assumed,
750	since `Scheme.Pic0Scheme` carries `[Scheme.HasPicScheme C]` — so the count does not shrink
751	here either. What it buys is that every obligation is of the ordinary kind.
752	
753	Both are kept: this one records what the `picSharp` route reaches over `k̄`, and the
754	headline states what the project claims over an arbitrary field. -/
755	noncomputable def picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed [IsAlgClosed k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
756	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
757	    JacobianWitness C :=
758	  haveI := hasRationalPoint_of_curve_of_isAlgClosed C
759	  picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint C
760	
761	/-- Existence of an Albanese witness for every smooth proper geometrically irreducible
762	curve, uniformly in the genus via the Picard identity component `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
763	(`picardJacobianWitness`). This packages the five protected obligations (`Jacobian`,
764	`instGrpObj`, `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus`, `instIsProper`,
765	`instGeometricallyIrreducible`) into a single existence statement, and records that the
766	Albanese property of the underlying scheme `J` is uniform over every choice of
767	`k`-rational marked point `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C` (via the `isAlbaneseFor` field of
768	`JacobianWitness`). -/
769	theorem nonempty_jacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
770	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
771	    Nonempty (JacobianWitness C) :=
772	  ⟨picardJacobianWitness C⟩
773	
774	/-- A choice of Albanese witness for `C`, extracted via `Classical.choice`.
775	Used to define `Jacobian C` and to discharge each of the four protected instances
776	on it. -/
777	noncomputable def jacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
778	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
779	    JacobianWitness C :=
780	  Classical.choice (nonempty_jacobianWitness C)
781	
782	-- data
783	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`.
784	
785	The Jacobian is the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness for `C` (see
786	`JacobianWitness` and `nonempty_jacobianWitness`), so it is `Pic⁰_{C/k}` in its étale
787	form for the witness `picardJacobianWitness`, whose remaining content is the five
788	obligations enumerated in the file header: the two étale leaves of §"The open leaves of
789	the two witnesses" together with `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` and the two residues
790	`Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced` / `Pic0Et.universallyClosed`. The genus-`0`
791	specialisation is implicit in the witness — a smooth proper geometrically
792	irreducible group scheme over `k` of relative dimension `0` is `Spec k` — so
793	no separate genus-`0` construction is needed. -/
794	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
795	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
796	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
797	  (jacobianWitness C).J
798	
799	namespace Jacobian
800	
801	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
802	
803	-- data
804	/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
805	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) := (jacobianWitness C).grpObj
806	
807	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is smooth of relative dimension `g` over `k`, where `g` is the
808	genus of `C`. -/
809	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
810	  (jacobianWitness C).smoothGenus
811	
812	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is proper over `k`. -/
813	instance instIsProper : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom := (jacobianWitness C).proper
814	
815	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
816	instance instGeometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
817	  (jacobianWitness C).geomIrred
818	
819	end Jacobian

461	The number `genus C` in leaf B is not an arbitrary index: it is the dimension of the
462	Zariski tangent space of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` at the identity
463	(`Scheme.Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne`, the Kleiman §5 Thm 5.11
464	chain through the truncated-exponential splitting and the Mayer–Vietoris comparison).
465	Since `genus C` is by definition `dim_k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`, the two sides match with no
466	transport, exactly as leaf C's `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed` matches
467	`Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property`.
468	
469	That chain is **not landed** — an earlier version of this docstring called it "landed
470	mathematics", contradicting what this very declaration records below, that its axioms
471	carry `sorryAx`. Both legs of it are proved; the residue is one statement,
472	`Pic0.semilinearComparison_cotangentSpaceDual_h1Cok`. Corrected 2026-07-29 (`ajc-p2`).
473	
474	Stating it here fixes what leaf B still owes, which is easy to misjudge from the leaf
475	alone. It is *not* the dimension count. It is the two steps that turn a tangent-space
476	dimension into a relative dimension:
477	
478	1. `Scheme.Pic0.smooth` — bare smoothness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` over `k`, itself `sorry`-bodied
479	   upstream, so leaf B presupposes an obligation rather than reducing one. That obligation
480	   is smaller than it looks, and worth stating here because it changes what a reader should
481	   expect to have to build: its *entire* remaining content is
482	   `GeometricallyReduced (Pic⁰_{C/k}).hom`. Mathlib's public `smooth_of_grpObj` takes
483	   `[LocallyOfFiniteType f]`, `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` and `[GeometricallyReduced f]` and
484	   returns `Smooth f` over an arbitrary field, so the translation argument that propagates
485	   smoothness from the identity is already done there; the first two inputs are landed
486	   (`Pic0.locallyOfFiniteType`, `Pic0.grpObj`) and elaborate at these hypotheses verbatim,
487	   while `GeometricallyReduced` does not synthesize and its only producer in the tree is
488	   `Smooth.geometricallyReduced`, which would be circular. So `Pic0.smooth` is Cartier's
489	   theorem in characteristic zero and a genuine characteristic-`p` statement otherwise —
490	   not a translation argument. "Entire remaining content" is meant strictly, and it is
491	   measured rather than estimated: the conclusion of `Pic0.smooth`, proved at that
492	   theorem's binders verbatim with `GeometricallyReduced` as the sole added hypothesis, is
493	   **axiom-clean** — `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, where `Pic0.smooth` itself
494	   reports `sorryAx`. So supplying geometric reducedness discharges it outright, with no
495	   residual leak elsewhere in the assembly;
496	2. the passage from "smooth, with `dim_{κ(e)} T_e = n`" to
497	   `SmoothOfRelativeDimension n`. Mathlib defines the latter by local standard-smooth
498	   presentations, not by a tangent-space dimension. There *is* a bridge, but it is at the
499	   algebra level and it goes through a different invariant:
500	   `Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.iff_of_isStandardSmooth` characterises
501	   relative dimension `n` as `Module.rank S Ω[S⁄R] = n`, the rank of the module of Kähler
502	   differentials. So the missing mathematics is (i) the identification of that rank with
503	   the tangent-space dimension at the identity — over a field these are dual to one
504	   another, but the statement has to be made and the duality is where a rank/`finrank`
505	   mismatch would bite — and (ii) the passage from an affine-local statement about
506	   presentations to the scheme-level class, which quantifies over an affine cover of
507	   `Pic⁰_{C/k}` rather than over a single point.
508	
509	   This is worth stating precisely rather than as "no bridge exists", which an earlier
510	   version of this docstring claimed: the leaf's cost is a translation between two
511	   invariants of smoothness, not the construction of one from nothing.
512	
513	Like `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed`, this is a faithful record of a distance rather
514	than a discharge: its axioms carry `sorryAx`, because the dimension chain it invokes
515	still rests on `Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpaceDual_eq_finrank_h1Cok`. -/
516	theorem finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
517	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
518	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
519	    [Scheme.HasPicScheme C] [Scheme.PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C] :
520	    Module.finrank
521	        (IsLocalRing.ResidueField
522	          ((Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).left.presheaf.stalk
523	            ((Scheme.Pic0.identitySection C).base default)))
524	        (IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace
525	          ((Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).left.presheaf.stalk
526	            ((Scheme.Pic0.identitySection C).base default)))
527	      = genus C :=
528	  Scheme.Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne C
529	
530	/-- **Leaf C: the Albanese universal property, over an arbitrary field and every point.**
531	
532	`Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property` proves exactly this statement, but under two
533	restrictions the witness cannot accept: the base field is algebraically closed, and the
534	genus is positive. The witness needs the property over the ambient field `k` and for
535	*every* choice of `k`-rational marked point `P`, including `genus C = 0` (where
536	`Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k` and the content is the classical rigidity statement that every
537	pointed morphism from a genus-`0` curve to an abelian variety is constant).
538	
539	Descending the algebraically-closed case to `k` is the Galois-descent step of the
540	campaign's cluster `G`; the genus-`0` case is Mumford §4 rigidity.
541	
542	`isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed` below is the same statement in the case the landed
543	proof covers, and it is a theorem rather than a leaf: it shows the *only* content this
544	leaf adds over the landed `Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property`, beyond the two
545	restrictions named above, is the basepoint condition. -/
546	theorem isAlbanese_pic0 (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
547	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
548	    [Scheme.HasPicScheme C] [Scheme.PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]
549	    (grp : GrpObj (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C)) (pr : IsProper (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).hom)
550	    (sm : Smooth (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).hom)
551	    (gi : GeometricallyIrreducible (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).hom)
552	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
553	    @IsAlbanese k _ C P (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C) grp pr sm gi :=
554	  sorry
555	
556	/-- **Leaf C, étale formulation: the Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`.**
557	
558	The same statement as `isAlbanese_pic0`, for the identity component of the scheme
559	representing the étale-sheafified functor — over an arbitrary base field, for every
560	`k`-rational marked point, and with **no hypothesis on `C(k)`**.
561	
562	Its content over the landed `Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property` is the three
563	pieces recorded on `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed`: arbitrary base field in place of
564	algebraically closed (the Galois-descent step of cluster `G`), `genus C = 0` as well as
565	positive genus (Mumford §4 rigidity), and the basepoint condition `P ≫ ι_P = η`. To those
566	the étale formulation adds the same transport `isAlbanese_pic0` does not need: the landed
567	Abel–Jacobi morphism `Pic0.abelJacobi` is constructed for `Pic0Scheme`, and carrying it
568	to `Pic0SchemeEt` is part of this leaf.
569	
570	Note that the marked point `P` appears here as an argument, not as a hypothesis on `C`:
571	`IsAlbanese` is a statement *about* a pointing, and `JacobianWitness.isAlbaneseFor`
572	quantifies over all of them. That is exactly why the headline needs no rational point —
573	the witness scheme `J` is intrinsic to `C`, and only the universal morphism depends on a
574	choice of `P`, in the same way `Challenge.lean` binds a point only in
575	`AbelJacobi.Jacobian.ofCurve`. -/
576	theorem isAlbanese_pic0Et (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
577	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
578	    (grp : GrpObj (Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C)) (pr : IsProper (Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C).hom)
579	    (sm : Smooth (Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C).hom)
580	    (gi : GeometricallyIrreducible (Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C).hom)
581	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
582	    @IsAlbanese k _ C P (Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C) grp pr sm gi :=
583	  sorry
584	
585	/-- **Leaf C in the case the landed proof covers**, over an algebraically closed field and
586	in positive genus, with the basepoint condition as an explicit hypothesis.
587	
588	This is a theorem, and it is the honest measure of the distance between
589	`isAlbanese_pic0` and the Albanese development. The factorisation clause of `IsAlbanese`

thing — `SymPowData C g` for `g ≥ 2`, the missing scheme quotient — rather than six
entangled gaps.

Milne's proof turns the Albanese equation `φ = aj ≫ ψ` into the symmetric-power

`Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean` proves Milne Proposition III.6.1 over the
symmetric-power interface in an arbitrary cartesian monoidal category. This file
instantiates it at the object the challenge cares about: `J = Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` for a
smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve `C` over an algebraically closed field.

The point of the instantiation is that **every hypothesis of the general theorem is
discharged here except one**. Specifically:

* `IsCommMonObj (Pic0.jacobianScheme C)` and `IsCommMonObj A` — Milne §I.1 Corollary
  1.4, now available on the project's four-instance package
  (`isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package`, `Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`).
* **pointed rigidity** for `Pic⁰ ⟶ A` — Milne §I.1 Corollary 1.2, likewise
  (`isMonHom_of_pointed`). This is the `hom` input, and it rests on the sorry-free
  rigidity chain of `RigidityLemma.lean`.
* the connector in both directions, and the assembly — proved in
  `Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean`.

What is **not** discharged, and is the entire remaining content of this leg:

> `SymPowData C (genus C)` — the `g`-th symmetric power of the curve, with its
> symmetrisation projection and universal property,

together with the cycle map presented as the symmetrisation of a pointed Abel–Jacobi
map (`hf`, `haj0`) and the descent datum, which `Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean` §2
reduces to a morphism on a dense open (Milne III.5.1(a) birationality).

* `Pic0.albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData` — the Albanese universal property
  of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`, with the symmetric power as an explicit argument. Axiom-clean

`Pic0.jacobianScheme C` is built from `Pic0.bundle`, which routes through the Picard
representability seam; at a *synthesis site* that seam still reports `sorryAx`
(the five obligations named on the AJC team thread, none of them in this leg). So this
theorem is **not** a closed result about the actual Jacobian, and must not be reported
as one. What it does establish is sharp and worth stating precisely:

> the Albanese *argument* is complete. Given the symmetric power, Milne III.6.1 holds
> for `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` with no further input from this leg.

That is a different claim from `albanese_universal_property` in
`Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean`, which quantifies over a `sorry`-bodied `abelJacobi` and a
`sorry`-bodied `SymmetricPower` and therefore asserts nothing about either.

## References

Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.6 Proposition 6.1, p. 104; §I.1 Corollaries 1.2 and
1.4. Blueprint `thm:albanese_universal_property`.

import AlgebraicJacobian.AbelianVariety.Rigidity
import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Grp

/-!
# Corollaries of the rigidity lemma

This file proves the engine application of the rigidity lemma (Milne, *Abelian Varieties*,
I Cor 1.2; Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, §II.4 p. 44, Corollary 1): a **pointed** morphism of
group schemes whose source is proper and geometrically integral over an algebraically closed
field is a **homomorphism** of group objects.

## Main result

* `AlgebraicGeometry.isMonHom_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`: let `K` be an
  algebraically closed field, `A` a monoid object of `Over (Spec K)` that is proper and
  geometrically integral, and `B` a group object that is separated and locally of finite type.
  Any morphism `g : A ⟶ B` with `η[A] ≫ g = η[B]` satisfies `IsMonHom g`, i.e. commutes with
  the multiplications.

  Since a monoid homomorphism of group objects automatically commutes with inversion
  (`CategoryTheory.inv_hom` in mathlib), for `A` a group object this is the full statement
  "a pointed morphism of group schemes is a homomorphism of group schemes".

## Proof sketch

Following Milne (I Cor 1.2), consider the "defect" morphism

`φ := (μ[A] ≫ g) / ((fst A A ≫ g) * (snd A A ≫ g)) : A ⊗ A ⟶ B`,

written in the group `Hom(A ⊗ A, B)` (mathlib's `MonObj.Hom.group`); pointwise it is
`φ(x, y) = g(x·y) · (g(x)·g(y))⁻¹`. Both slice restrictions `φ(·, e)` and `φ(e, ·)`
collapse to the unit point of `B` (using `g(e) = e`), so the rigidity lemma
(`exists_unique_eq_snd_comp_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`, with `X = Y = A`,
`y₀ = η[A]`, `z₀ = η[B]`) factors `φ` as `snd A A ≫ ψ`; restricting along the *other*
slice `{e} × A` identifies `ψ = 1`, so `φ = 1`, which is exactly `IsMonHom.mul_hom`.

Compared to Milne's statement the hypothesis set is honest and slightly weaker: `A` only
needs a monoid structure (no inverses, no smoothness), and `B` can be any separated, locally
of finite type group scheme over `K` (no properness, connectedness or commutativity).
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K]

/-- **A pointed morphism of group schemes is a homomorphism** (Milne, *Abelian Varieties*,
I Cor 1.2; Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, §II.4 p. 44, Corollary 1). Let `K` be an
algebraically closed field, `A` a monoid object of `Over (Spec K)` whose underlying scheme is
proper and geometrically integral over `K`, and `B` a group object whose underlying scheme is
separated and locally of finite type over `K`. If `g : A ⟶ B` is pointed (`η[A] ≫ g = η[B]`),
then `g` is a homomorphism of monoid objects.

For `A` a group object this makes `g` a homomorphism of group objects: a monoid homomorphism
automatically commutes with inversion (`CategoryTheory.inv_hom`). -/
theorem isMonHom_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral
    {A B : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} [MonObj A] [GrpObj B]
    [IsProper A.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral A.hom]
    [IsSeparated B.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType B.hom]
    (g : A ⟶ B) (hg : η[A] ≫ g = η[B]) : IsMonHom g := by
  -- the defect morphism `φ(x, y) = g(x·y) · (g(x)·g(y))⁻¹` in the group `Hom(A ⊗ A, B)`
  set φ : A ⊗ A ⟶ B := (μ[A] ≫ g) / ((fst A A ≫ g) * (snd A A ≫ g)) with hφdef
  -- `φ` contracts the slice `A × {e}` to the unit point of `B`
  have e1 : lift (𝟙 A) (toUnit A ≫ η[A]) ≫ μ[A] ≫ g = g := by
    rw [← Category.assoc, MonObj.lift_comp_one_right, Category.id_comp]
  have e2 : lift (𝟙 A) (toUnit A ≫ η[A]) ≫ fst A A ≫ g = g := by
    rw [lift_fst_assoc, Category.id_comp]
  have e3 : lift (𝟙 A) (toUnit A ≫ η[A]) ≫ snd A A ≫ g = 1 := by
    rw [lift_snd_assoc, Category.assoc, hg, ← Hom.one_def]
  have hslice : lift (𝟙 A) (toUnit A ≫ η[A]) ≫ φ = toUnit A ≫ η[B] := by
    rw [hφdef, GrpObj.comp_div, MonObj.comp_mul, e1, e2, e3, _root_.mul_one, div_self',
      Hom.one_def]
  -- rigidity: `φ` factors through the second projection
  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ, -⟩ := exists_unique_eq_snd_comp_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral
    φ η[A] η[B] hslice
  -- restricting along the slice `{e} × A` identifies the factor with the unit
  have hψ1 : ψ = (1 : A ⟶ B) := by
    have h1 : lift (toUnit A ≫ η[A]) (𝟙 A) ≫ φ = ψ := by
      rw [hψ, lift_snd_assoc, Category.id_comp]
    have f1 : lift (toUnit A ≫ η[A]) (𝟙 A) ≫ μ[A] ≫ g = g := by
      rw [← Category.assoc, MonObj.lift_comp_one_left, Category.id_comp]
    have f2 : lift (toUnit A ≫ η[A]) (𝟙 A) ≫ fst A A ≫ g = 1 := by
      rw [lift_fst_assoc, Category.assoc, hg, ← Hom.one_def]
    have f3 : lift (toUnit A ≫ η[A]) (𝟙 A) ≫ snd A A ≫ g = g := by
      rw [lift_snd_assoc, Category.id_comp]
    rw [← h1, hφdef, GrpObj.comp_div, MonObj.comp_mul, f1, f2, f3, _root_.one_mul, div_self']
  -- hence the defect vanishes identically
  have hφ1 : φ = (1 : A ⊗ A ⟶ B) := by rw [hψ, hψ1, MonObj.comp_one]
  rw [hφdef, div_eq_one] at hφ1
  -- and `μ[A] ≫ g = (g ⊗ₘ g) ≫ μ[B]`
  have h2 : (g ⊗ₘ g) ≫ μ[B] = (fst A A ≫ g) * (snd A A ≫ g) := by
    rw [MonObj.mul_eq_mul B, MonObj.comp_mul, tensorHom_fst, tensorHom_snd]
